# Mini-Core

Run `./minicore run FILE` with Python 3.13. No packages or build step are required.

- `minicore` checks ASCII and tokenizes the whole input, then uses recursive descent to parse the grammar. The checker infers monomorphic types by unifying a graph of types and unknowns. After all equations have been imposed, a cycle check rejects infinite types, including those in unused bindings.
- `mcvm.py` compiles the AST to stack instructions. Each variable reference resolves to a local slot or an indexed group of captured values. A group snapshots selected slots from one enclosing activation; inner closures can share inherited groups without copying each captured value at every level. Recursive closures get their own self slot. Non-tail calls save a continuation on a Python list; tail calls just replace the current activation.
- `mcfast.py` lowers small bytecode programs to a Python loop over basic blocks, preserving the explicit stacks. This avoids per-instruction dispatch on compute-heavy loops. The generated code uses only fixed templates, compiler indices and known operators; source identifiers and literals are never pasted into Python code. Larger programs use the ordinary bytecode evaluator.

Run `python3 tests/run.py` for the CLI tests (including the provided examples and limit cases) and deterministic differential tests. The latter compare generated programs against a separate substitution-based typechecker and a direct evaluator, exercising both execution paths.
